issue.title: Provide validated CI wait commands that fail when polling never produces a parsed state
issue.description: Proposed by sase-1kl.4 note #7; monitor fze4qmnv7vpr printed jq parse errors for 4h32m and exited 0. tools/release_watch addresses sase release waiting only. Design a small validated CI-run wait helper or an opt-in polling contract with a bounded consecutive-read failure policy, inline preflight, observable state, and tests for malformed queries, authentication failure, timeout, and valid state changes. Do not infer failure from arbitrary monitor prose or change every shell command exit code. No semantic duplicate in task search or last-week sweep; general monitor epic sase-kp does not establish a regression cause.

task_type_fields.proposal: Provide a reusable CI wait entry point or explicit validated-poll contract that cannot report success without parsing a workflow state. Retain command evidence and fail promptly after repeated malformed reads.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic sase-1kx builds a release-specific stdlib watcher. General monitor semantics and reusable arbitrary CI waits need their own design; this incident predates the epic.

issue.creation_reason: A prior release monitor spent 4h32m polling malformed jq and then exited zero. The release-specific watcher now covers this release, but generic CI waits can still silently do no useful work.

payload.description: Validated polling is an adjacent opt-in capability for monitors, not evidence of a regression in the monitor lifecycle epic
